help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Researchers suppose that music activates several areas of the brain simultaneously.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: A Canadian research group was able to show that the release does not begin at the moment of the musical climax but a few seconds before.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: belegen signals an established finding; vermuten marks a supposition.
help.tips[0].en.text: Forscher vermuten / nehmen an / gehen davon aus (supposition) vs Studien belegen / zeigen / haben nachgewiesen (assertion). The question 'Was vermuten die Forscher?' wants the supposition, not the proven part.
help.tips[0].en.title: Assertion vs supposition
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Interestingly, the brain releases dopamine – much as when eating a favourite dish.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Research here is only at the beginning – and music is, as so often, a good way ahead of it.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: allerdings plus fehlen bisher marks the limit of the research; vergleichbar mit introduces the comparison, not the caveat.
help.tips[1].en.text: ähnlich wie / vergleichbar mit / genau wie beim … (comparison — 'Womit wird … verglichen?'). Die Forschung steht noch am Anfang / bisher fehlen Belege / offen bleibt (caveat — 'Wie steht es um die Forschung?').
help.tips[1].en.title: The comparison and the caveat
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Astonishingly, the effect also appears in people who never learnt an instrument.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The brain apparently rewards the expectation.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: Sentence adverbs in -erweise like bemerkenswerterweise flag what the author finds notable; hedges would be vermutlich or offenbar.
help.tips[2].en.text: interessanterweise, bemerkenswerterweise, erstaunlicherweise (notable), vermutlich, offenbar (hedges), allerdings, freilich (caveats). Underline them: they mark the sentences the questions come from.
help.tips[2].en.title: Sentence adverbs flag the author's stance
help.hookEn: Read a popular-science article on why music moves us and tell what researchers have shown from what they only suspect.
help.introEn: A popular-science text on why music moves us — researchers' suppositions (Forscher vermuten, dass …), a mechanism (das Gehirn schüttet Dopamin aus), a comparison (ähnlich wie beim Essen), a further surprise (erstaunlicherweise …), practical applications, and a caveat about the state of research (die Forschung steht erst am Anfang). Science pages are full of texts like this; the skill is separating what is asserted from what is supposed (vermuten, nahelegen, es scheint) and catching the comparison and the caveat, which carry the real information. The vocabulary is the module's: vermuten, aktivieren, zuständig für, ausschütten, vergleichbar mit, am Anfang stehen — and the sentence adverb interessanterweise, which signals the fact the author finds most notable.
help.rememberEn[0]: vermuten ≠ belegen: sort every claim by its verb.
help.rememberEn[1]: Comparison (ähnlich wie) and caveat (am Anfang stehen) are the question targets.
help.examEn: Popular-science texts with detail questions are a standard reading text in the C1 exam — and in every weekend newspaper.
